header:
Date: 2026-03-13 | Time: 16:00 PDT | Duration: ~48 min
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Ethan Brooks (Redwood Solutions), Daniel Reyes (CTO - Horizon Edge), Maya Li (Head of ML - Horizon Edge), Omar Khan (Cloud Infra Lead - Horizon Edge)
summary: Intro/partner discovery to explore integration options: private/dedicated deployments, managed GPU offerings, pilot/benchmark plan, security and compliance questions (VPC, KMS, SOC2), and commercial model. Agreed to share runbook and sample workload and schedule pilot kickoff week of 2026-03-30.
topics: Deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00:00] Sofia Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We really appreciate you taking the time. Quick round intro?
[00:00:08] Daniel Reyes: Yeah, Daniel here, CTO at Horizon Edge. We run an edge cloud for video inference, building some LLM driven metadata pipelines.
[00:00:15] Maya Li: Maya, Head of ML. We're evaluating partners for managed inference - both on our dedicated infra and potentially co-managed private deployments.
[00:00:20] Omar Khan: Omar, infra. I'll be the technical contact for networking and security.
[00:00:25] Sofia Patel: Great. From Redwood: Priya, Ethan and me. Priya will lead the tech details.
[00:00:30] Priya Kapoor: Hi all. Quick agenda: 1) understand your workload and constraints, 2) deployment options and performance/cost tradeoffs, 3) security/compliance, 4) next steps/pilot. Sound ok?
[00:00:40] Daniel Reyes: Yep sounds good.
[00:01:05] Priya Kapoor: Can you give us a sense of current infra and what you're trying to solve? GPUs, latency targets, throughput?
[00:01:12] Maya Li: Sure. We run mixed workloads: short chat-style prompts for metadata enrichment (latency target ~200-300ms p50), and longer batch summarization jobs for nightly processing. We currently use a mix of A100 clusters on-prem and some H100 in cloud for experimental stuff. Cost is a big driver; latency is important but we can tolerate a bit more tail if cost drops.
[00:01:45] Omar Khan: Network is private VPC, we have strict egress rules and KMS keys for our data. We also need SSO and RBAC integrations. SOC2 is in flight.
[00:01:55] Priya Kapoor: Good — that's typical. So two main personas: online low-latency and batch throughput. Redwood can serve both: hosted for fastest onboarding, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) for strict security.
[00:02:18] Ethan Brooks: One note: our runtime supports continuous batching and prefix/KV caching which can help the chat-style cases to hit lower cost while keeping latency SLOs.
[00:02:28] Maya Li: How mature is the KV cache? We do a lot of similar prefixes.
[00:02:33] Priya Kapoor: We've had it in production for a while; it stores repeated prefixes and reuses KV cache across requests when policy allows. It's not magic — depends on prompt patterns — but customers often see 20-60% token cost reduction for chat-heavy workloads.
[00:02:52] Daniel Reyes: Interesting. We also have questions about quantization — we saw 4-bit runs improve cost but worried about quality regressions. Does Redwood provide guidance?
[00:03:05] Priya Kapoor: Yes. Redwood Optimize gives model and quantization recommendations per workload. We typically run controlled A/Bs against a holdout prompt set. For many transformer models, 4-bit quant (LLM.int8/4 variants) retains quality for many workloads but we validate with evals.
[00:03:25] Omar Khan: From a security perspective, can Redwood run inside our VPC, use our KMS, and produce audit logs?
[00:03:33] Sofia Patel: Absolutely. Our Private deployment can be customer VPC or on-prem. We integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management, provide audit logs and support RBAC + SAML SSO. We also have SOC 2 Type II docs and can share them.
[00:03:45] Maya Li: Great — please send the SOC2 docs.
[00:03:48] Sofia Patel: Will do.
[00:04:05] Priya Kapoor: On performance — what's your p50/p95 targets again for online?
[00:04:10] Maya Li: p50 ~ 200-300ms, p95 below 800ms ideally.
[00:04:15] Priya Kapoor: Ok, good. If you want those latencies on large open models we usually recommend Dedicated pools with pinned model variants for predictability and low tail latency. For best latency/cost balance, we can recommend model family + quantization profile and kernel selection tuned for your sequence lengths.
[00:04:33] Daniel Reyes: Kernel selection? Like auto choose kernels for H100 vs A100?
[00:04:38] Ethan Brooks: Yes, runtime picks optimized kernels based on model arch and hardware. On H100 you'll see different performance characteristics. We also expose kernel/compilation logs in the Console for diagnostics.
[00:04:49] Omar Khan: Any examples on throughput numbers per GPU?
[00:04:52] Priya Kapoor: It depends heavily on model, sequence length, batch. For a 70B dense model at 128 tokens, on A100 you'd get X tokens/s and on H100 more; we'll share benchmark sheets. For planning let's run a pilot with your sample prompts and measure end-to-end latency including network from your VPC.
[00:05:10] Maya Li: We want to see both cost per 1M tokens and latency percentiles.
[00:05:14] Priya Kapoor: Agreed. We'll provide scripts to run locally which hit our endpoints or the private deployment and produce the token and latency breakdown.
[00:05:30] Daniel Reyes: Commercially, what's the model — is it usage-based on hosted, reserved pricing for Dedicated, and enterprise licensing for Private?
[00:05:36] Sofia Patel: Exactly. Hosted is usage-based. Dedicated is reserved capacity (monthly/annual commits) with SLA. Private is an enterprise license/fee plus support. We can share indicative pricing bands.
[00:05:50] Maya Li: How do rollouts work — can we do canary and automatic fallback to smaller models if capacity spikes?
[00:05:56] Ethan Brooks: Yes — our routing layer supports policy-based routing with canary and automatic fallback to compatible model variants by policy (latency, cost, region).
[00:06:06] Omar Khan: For the private deployment, is network egress fully controlled? Data residency?
[00:06:11] Sofia Patel: Yes — private control plane and customer-managed networking. Data residency is supported via region pinning and on-prem option for full control.
[00:06:20] Daniel Reyes: One of our concerns is vendor lock-in. If we go with Redwood Private, how portable are models and configs?
[00:06:26] Priya Kapoor: We try to be standards-friendly — model files are standard HF formats, config as JSON/yaml, and runbooks to rehydrate a deployment. Still, some runtime optimizations (compiled kernels) won't be trivially portable, but we document them.
[00:06:40] Maya Li: Ok. Another question: can Redwood run in a multi-tenant setup inside our infra so we can share capacity across teams?
[00:06:47] Sofia Patel: Yes — Dedicated pools can be segmented with RBAC and per-route quotas; Private installations support tenanting at the traffic plane if you want logical separation.
[00:06:58] Omar Khan: For pilot scope, we'd like a small Dedicated pool or Private single-node with H100 / A100 parity to test both latency and batch. We can provide sample datasets.
[00:07:07] Priya Kapoor: Sounds perfect. Proposed pilot: 2-week run, targeted tests: latency p50/p95, cost per 1M tokens, quality A/B vs your baseline, and failure/fallback behavior. We'll instrument Console dashboards for you.
[00:07:20] Daniel Reyes: That works. We'll lock down a small window week of 2026-03-30.
[00:07:24] Sofia Patel: Great — action items: we'll share SOC2, one-pager, pricing bands; Priya will share benchmark scripts and runbook; Maya please share sample prompts + access for test harness.
[00:07:35] Maya Li: Yep will do.
[00:07:44] Priya Kapoor: Quick note on integration patterns: if you want to keep inference in your VPC, we can deploy a Private control plane with connectors; if you want Redwood managed but data isolated we support dedicated-hosted with VPC peering. We'll sketch both in the doc.
[00:07:59] Omar Khan: SAML/SSO integration — we use Okta.
[00:08:03] Sofia Patel: We support Okta, SAML, and fine-grained RBAC.
[00:08:10] Ethan Brooks: I'll attach a sample infra diagram and the Console screenshots for routing and dashboards.
[00:08:18] Daniel Reyes: Any blockers or common gotchas you've seen on private deployments?
[00:08:22] Priya Kapoor: Mostly network egress rules and keys — getting KMS integrated early avoids delays. Also, planning for GPU provisioning lead time matters — H100 capacity can be constrained in some regions.
[00:08:35] Maya Li: Understood.
[00:08:42] Sofia Patel: Competitors — anything you evaluated already?
[00:08:45] Daniel Reyes: We looked at NVIDIA Cloud and Lambda; cost/perf tradeoffs looked close.
[00:08:50] Sofia Patel: Good to know. We'll highlight differentiators (unified runtime, cost-optimization tooling, rollout controls).
[00:08:58] Priya Kapoor: Ok last bit: success criteria for pilot?
[00:09:03] Maya Li: Demonstrate p50 < 300ms for online, p95 < 800ms, and cost per 1M tokens within 15% of our target benchmark. Also operational: RBAC/SSO working and KMS integration validated.
[00:09:18] Priya Kapoor: Perfect, we'll codify that.
[00:09:25] Sofia Patel: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with materials and calendar invite for pilot kickoff.
[00:09:31] Daniel Reyes: Thanks all, appreciate it.
[00:09:34] [meeting ends]
